image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Six-storey Thai rental apartment block, pale cream painted concrete frame with a grid of identical shallow balconies on every upper floor, each balcony with a pale green railing, an aluminium sliding door, a wall-mounted air-conditioning condenser and a laundry rack of hanging clothes, open ground floor on square columns used as motorcycle parking beside a small glass lobby door, a vertical strip of frosted stairwell windows at one end, flat roof with a parapet and a row of blue plastic water tanks, a painted name signboard across the ground-floor beam Materials: cream painted render with grey rain streaks below every balcony, pale green powder-coated steel railings, anodised aluminium door frames, bare grey concrete columns at ground level, chalky blue polyethylene water tanks.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90: silhouette 0.95 on a band table at 0.013 / 0.008 of height, structure 0.93 with every identity feature present at the plate's count and position, form 0.88, material 0.86 and lighting 0.86 held down by the flat harness light and the invented -Z / +X elevations. 27,904/32,000 triangles, 16/24 draw calls, 12/16 materials, 16/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Four bays of 3.10 m between 0.60 m piers, five rows at 2.58 m from a beam top at 4.15, as forty real holes 1.10 m deep through two facade extrusions; a thirteen-baluster pale-green railing, a sliding door left, a condenser with its pipe right and a laundry rail in every one; garments of four sizes on twenty of them. Band table against the proxy: mean |delta width| 0.013 of height.
featureReviews.notes: Bay pitch, pier width and row pitch were read off the proxy's +Z depth map at 53.9 px/m rather than the plate, which foreshortens the front; the proxy dropped a row (four at 3.25 m) and the plate's five railing rows at a 111 px pitch decided the count. The first build's laundry was three equal navy/white/red panels and read as French flags; the garments are now four different widths and heights in muted tones with per-instance tints. The recess back walls carry a 0.63 linear vertex tint (the plate measures them at #ABA99D in shadow against #D4CDBD), which is what makes the grid read as recesses under the harness's flat light.

featureReviews.evidence: Open ground floor 0.25..3.60 on eleven 0.45 m columns under a 0.55 m beam that wraps the +X corner, a cream core wall 5.9 m back, a recessed lobby with a double glass door facing -X, and APARTMENT baked across the beam centred at x=1.5 -- right of centre, where the plate's word sits at 0.556 of the front width.
featureReviews.notes: The -X wall is solid to the plinth for the rear 6.4 m (proxy side map: x 5..350 px of 635) and open forward of it, which is where the plate's lobby door sits behind a corner column. The turntable gate passes with no enclosed background on any azimuth: the colonnade always shows the core or lobby wall behind it, never the backdrop. No motorcycles -- an exterior shell.

featureReviews.evidence: Six six-pane frosted windows in one strip at z -1.70..-0.05 on -X, one per floor including ground; six ribbed blue tanks in two tight rows on the rear-centre of the roof with caps at the declared 19.00; outlined render panels per floor and column on -X, +X and the parapet bands.
featureReviews.notes: Strip position from the proxy side map (4.45..6.10 m from the rear face); tank cluster x-range from the proxy's top occupancy row (0.25..0.72 of width). The proxy's parapet reads 0.038 wider than this model's in band 8 -- a coping overhang the plate does not clearly show and that was not built.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve materials, nine measured off the plate at PBR confidence 0.636-0.860; cream #D4CDBD render, #9C9C98 concrete, #A6C8B0 railing, #6D88A6 tanks; rain wash as an alpha canvas under every balcony; curtain stripes on the door glass.
featureReviews.notes: The railing crop (#74786A) is bars mixed with the shadowed recess, so the bar tone was read off the bay zoom instead; the glass is authored above its measured #606453 so forty recessed panes clear the hole gate. The streaks were first drawn as 26 heavy smears per bay and read as a fringe; the plate has a few faint ones at the post bases, and that is what ships.

name: Bangkok Apartment Block
nameTh: อพาร์ตเมนต์ 6 ชั้น
notes: The everyday Bangkok soi rental block (the kind that advertises rooms by the month) and the plainest of the four six-storey residential shells. Sizing: six floors at 3.0 m plus a 0.5 m ground-floor beam and a 0.5 m parapet gives 19 m; eight 2.5 m bays across gives 20 m wide, and a double-loaded corridor with 6 m deep rooms either side gives 14 m deep. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the open ground floor is a colonnade with a plain back wall behind it, not a parking level anyone can enter, and the sliding doors are tinted near-opaque panes rather than openings. The balcony module (slab, railing, door, condenser, laundry rack) repeats identically on every bay of five floors and is meant to be ONE instanced geometry; that is what keeps a 40-balcony facade inside the hero4x draw-call ceiling. The stairwell strip and the roof tanks are the only asymmetric features and are what stop it reading as a mirrored box. Balcony recesses and the ground-floor shadow zone must be authored above the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 or the silhouette gate reads them as holes. RESIZED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 1.259 : 0.816, and the plate agrees (front face ~500 px and side ~297 px against ~800 px of height at a ~35-degree three-quarter, which back-projects to w/h ~0.76 and d/w ~0.85). Height kept as the primary axis at 19.0 m, so w = 19.0/1.259 = 15.1 -> 15.0 and d = 15.0 x 0.816 = 12.2 -> 12.3. The earlier 20 x 14 was a bay-count estimate (eight 2.5 m bays); the plate shows FOUR bays of ~3.15 m between 0.6 m piers, and five balcony rows of 2.58 m over a 0.55 m beam whose top is at 4.15 m, deck at 17.05, parapet top at 18.5 and the tank caps at 19.0 -- all read off the proxy front and side depth maps at 53.9 px/m.
